newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa improving but not out of danger.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa improving but not out of danger.

text.p: Mother Teresa, who is recovering from heart surgery, continued to improve on Saturday but she is still not out of danger, a health bulletin by her doctors said.

"Mother Teresa's condition is improving. She is better than yesterday (Friday). But she is still not out of danger," a medical update by doctors in Calcutta's B.M. Birla Hearch Research Centre said. "She had good sleep last night. She said her morning prayers sitting on a chair around 0800 hours (0230 GMT) and she is looking cheerful," the bulletin said on Saturday.
Although seriously ill, the revered Roman Catholic nun, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her work among the poor and the destitute, has been asking to return home.
The 86-year-old nun on Friday jokingly asked her colleagues at the Missionaries of Charity, the religious order she founded, to send an ambulance to take her home.
But doctors have cautioned that her recovery will be slow and she might never be as active as before.

Mother Teresa, called the "Saint of the Gutters", had heart surgery on November 29 to clear two blocked coronary arteries. Her recovery has been delayed by an irregular heartbeat and long-standing lung and kidney trouble.
Doctors said on Wednesday they successfully regulated her heartbeat with a mild electric shock, but persistent bronchitis continued to hamper her recovery.
